what: Roblox is a platform where users, mostly young, play games made by other users. Players buy Robux, the in-game currency, and spend it inside those games; Roblox keeps a share and pays the rest to the creators.
customers: Over 80 million daily users worldwide, and the developers who build experiences on the platform.
money: virtual currency spent on items and experiences
moat: A network of creators and players that reinforce each other: more players attract more creators, and the creators build the content that keeps players coming back.
risks: It loses money, with a negative operating margin after paying creators and infrastructure costs
Child safety on the platform has drawn regulatory and legal scrutiny
Its audience skews young, which limits spending per user
Analyst targets imply the shares are already fully valued
opportunities: Revenue grew about 36% last year and about 30% a year over three years
Older users are a growing share of the audience and spend more
Advertising is a new revenue stream with much higher margins than the Robux split
watch: Daily active users and bookings per user, and progress toward profitability.
